correctness.rationale: Exact core-leaf update identities partition all \(4^n\) configurations by core weight into homogeneous and intermediate regimes. For even n, periodic pairs are exactly balanced-balanced pairs, and all nonhomogeneous periodic basins are singleton fixed or two-state orbits. For odd n, four disjoint weight-support types give \(2B(m+2)\) periodic ordered states; each target has exactly \(2^m\) direct preimages, producing basin \(2^{m+1}\) per two-cycle. Other states converge to one of two complement-exchanged homogeneous fixed points within three steps; explicit n>=4 witnesses attain three. Separate small-order n=2,3 cases give sharp bound two. Independent compressed Python enumeration checks n=2..8, and an adjacency-list C++ full-functional-graph census checks n=2..10, with 1,398,096 total C++ states and exact formula matching. Finite tests are corroboration, not infinite proofs; the all-order conclusion relies on the analytically exhaustive weight cases.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither matching one word (corona or majority) nor sharing a special n=2 member establishes implication. In the old sunlet law each core vertex sees two cycle neighbors and a leaf, unlike degree n core vertices here; the XOR law is linear and can have very different periods. The other majority graph families are not equivalent via a majority-preserving graph operation. No retrieved prior statement logically dominates the proposed all-n claim. Unseen general formulae for complete-graph corona threshold networks remain a priority risk.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison of claims distinguishes the known general two-period restriction from the new all-order individual basin counts, exact temporal orbit counts, sharp three-step bound and parity-dependent polynomial-versus-exponential oscillation asymptotics on \(K_n\circ K_1\). Primary sources inspected include the 2014 arXiv first-version text on unimodular/random-graph majority dynamics and the 2022 tree classification; the former proves a different graph-regime statement, and the latter covers the n=2 tree member only. Semantic record searches included graph aliases, exact formulas and stronger-coverage possibilities. No exact covering result was identified; historical unindexed equivalents remain a stated risk.
residual_risks: The original 1980 Goles–Olivos full text was inaccessible through the authorized literature route; the conclusion drawn from its available abstract is limited to general periodicity.
A graph-specific recurrence census may exist under an uncommon historical term (hairy clique, whiskered complete graph or threshold network). Semantic negative searches do not establish priority.
The same numerical central-binomial expressions occur in standard combinatorics under unrelated interpretations; novelty concerns their graph-dynamical interpretation and the basin/transient law.
All-order proof and finite checks are conducted within the same research process; no independent external audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The object \(K_n\circ K_1\) is the canonical one-private-leaf attachment to a clique, and exact two-cycle attraction probability is a meaningful stability invariant for synchronous opinion updating. The proof yields a complete classification of every recurrent orbit and each individual basin, sharp uniform transient depth, and a genuinely different asymptotic regime on alternate graph orders: even-n oscillatory basins have probability asymptotic to \(2/(\pi n)\), whereas odd-n basins have probability asymptotic to \(\sqrt{n/\pi}\,2^{-n/2}\). This polynomial-versus-exponential dichotomy is structural information not entailed by known general period-two results or by finite enumeration alone.
